sbh4.2:0.2: Higher Dhyānas, Formless Attainments, and Higher Knowledges
sbh4.2:1.1: The gross characteristic in all the lower planes, up through the sphere of nothingness, is in brief to be understood as twofold:
sbh4.2:1.2: that in the lower and lower planes one dwells in more suffering and [Restored: in less calm],
sbh4.2:1.4: This is the twofold gross characteristic.
sbh4.2:1.5: He investigates [it] by the six things, as appropriate,
sbh4.2:1.6: for whichever plane he wishes to become dispassionate toward; and, as appropriate, the calm characteristic of the [plane] above —
sbh4.2:1.7: up through the attention that is the fruit of practice-culmination. Here, 'secluded from sense-pleasures':
sbh4.2:2.1: Sense-pleasures are twofold: defilement-sense-pleasures and thing-sense-pleasures.
sbh4.2:2.2: [Conjectural: Seclusion from sense-pleasures] too is twofold: seclusion from association [with them] and seclusion from the object.
sbh4.2:2.3: 'Secluded from evil, unwholesome dharmas': [these are] the secondary defilements, the unwholesome dharmas caused by sense-pleasures — namely, bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct;
sbh4.2:2.4: taking up the rod, taking up the sword;
sbh4.2:2.5: quarrel, strife, contention, dispute, guile, deception, fraud and false speech — [these] come about.
sbh4.2:2.6: By the abandonment of these [he is] 'secluded from evil, unwholesome dharmas'. Because he does not [yet] see fault in [Conjectural: thought and examination], [it is] with wholesome *vitarka* and *vicāra* of its own plane that counter sense-pleasures —
sbh4.2:2.7: 'with *vitarka*, with *vicāra*'. The practice-culminating attention is seclusion from sense-pleasures. [What is] arisen immediately after it,
sbh4.2:2.8: caused by it, conditioned by it — therefore he says 'born of seclusion'. Because of attaining the desired, longed-for goal, because of not seeing fault in rapture,
sbh4.2:2.9: because of the disappearance of all encumbrance, and because of the abundant pliancy — the workability of mind and body — 'rapture-and-happiness', of one counting in order;
sbh4.2:2.10: and because he has for the first time risen out of the desire-realm — 'first'. From right contemplation of the object and from binding with one-pointed mindfulness — '*dhyāna*'. Because it is the fruit of practice-culmination — 'having attained'.
sbh4.2:2.11: And subsequently, from the accomplishment of cultivation and repeated practice — one who gains at will, one who gains without trouble, one who gains without difficulty — he passes a night in that *dhyāna* attainment, and a day too, as long as he wishes, up to seven days and nights. Therefore he says 'he dwells'.
sbh4.2:3.1: Turning the mind away from the [Restored: signs of the] *samādhi* with *vitarka* and *vicāra*,
sbh4.2:3.2: he binds it to the signs of the *samādhi* without *vitarka* and *vicāra*.
sbh4.2:3.3: Withdrawing [it] from the object that moves unsteadily,
sbh4.2:3.4: on an object that moves steadily the mind, calm and clear, proceeds [Restored: through its homogeneity];
sbh4.2:3.6: Therefore he says 'from the calming of *vitarka* and *vicāra*, from inward clarity'. Through repeated cultivation of that very *samādhi* without *vitarka* and *vicāra*, he passes beyond the stage [still] broken and interrupted [Restored: by these two] and reaches the unbroken, uninterrupted stage.
sbh4.2:3.7: Therefore he says 'from singleness of mind'. Because of the complete abandonment of *vitarka* and *vicāra* in every way, [it is] 'without *vitarka*, without *vicāra*'. *Samādhi* is the practice-culminating attention; [what follows] arises immediately after it, caused by it, conditioned by it.
sbh4.2:3.8: Therefore he says 'born of *samādhi*'. Because of attaining the desired, blameless goal, because of [Restored: not] seeing fault in rapture,
sbh4.2:3.9: [he is] in a state of rejoicing and [Conjectural: gladness]; because of the disappearance of all encumbrance of the defilement-side of the first *dhyāna* with its *vitarka* and *vicāra*, and because he is accompanied by [Conjectural: the happiness] of the pliancy — the workability of mind and body — that counters it:
sbh4.2:3.10: 'rapture-and-happiness'. 'The second', when counting in order. All the rest is to be understood as before.
sbh4.2:4.1: He sees fault in the signs of rapture.
sbh4.2:4.2: Therefore he says 'from dispassion toward rapture'.
sbh4.2:4.3: And at that time the twofold defect that agitates the mind has [Restored: disappeared]
sbh4.2:4.4: for one placing his mind in the raptureless third *dhyāna*:
sbh4.2:4.5: *vitarka* and *vicāra* [already] at the second *dhyāna*, and now rapture. Therefore he says 'he dwells equanimous'.
sbh4.2:4.6: For these two dharmas are agitators of the mind,
sbh4.2:4.8: Here, in the first *dhyāna* there are *vitarka* and *vicāra*,
sbh4.2:4.9: by which uninterrupted equanimity does not proceed.
sbh4.2:4.10: In the second *dhyāna* there is rapture,
sbh4.2:4.11: by which here too uninterrupted equanimity does not proceed.
sbh4.2:4.12: Therefore for this contemplator [equanimity] does not exist in the first and second *dhyāna*s; therefore it is said that in the third *dhyāna* 'he dwells equanimous'.
sbh4.2:4.13: Being equanimous, he dwells with mindfulness so established
sbh4.2:4.14: that those perceptions and attentions accompanied by rapture do [Conjectural: not] occur.
sbh4.2:4.15: If, however, through lack of cultivation of the third *dhyāna*, through a lapse of mindfulness, perceptions and attentions accompanied by rapture occasionally occur in his mind,
sbh4.2:4.16: he quickly penetrates them with wisdom;
sbh4.2:4.18: As they arise, he does not tolerate them;
sbh4.2:4.20: brings [them] to an end, and makes the mind indifferent [to them].
sbh4.2:5.1: For him who at that time dwells thus equanimous, mindful and clearly-knowing, through practice, [Restored: through cultivation,] through repeated practice, the [feeling] accompanied by rapture is abandoned —
sbh4.2:5.2: that which caused [Restored: exhilaration] of the mind — and a raptureless, calm, fully calmed feeling arises in his mind
sbh4.2:5.3: as the counterpart to rapture. At that time he experiences with the form-body and the mind-body happiness as feeling and happiness as pliancy. [Restored: Therefore he says 'and he experiences happiness with the body'.]
sbh4.2:5.5: there is no happiness of this kind, nor uninterrupted equanimity; above the third *dhyāna*, although equanimity is found,
sbh4.2:5.7: Because below it happiness and equanimity are absent, and above it happiness is absent,
sbh4.2:5.8: this is that sphere — the third *dhyāna* — of which the noble ones declare,
sbh4.2:5.9: with reference to the person who dwells in its attainment, '[Restored: equanimous,] mindful, dwelling in happiness, he dwells having attained the third *dhyāna*'. 'Noble ones', moreover, are [Restored: the Buddhas and the Buddhas' disciples].
sbh4.2:6.1: Here, because the antidote is [Conjectural: of the same kind],
sbh4.2:6.2: the antidote for abandoning happiness is not stated;
sbh4.2:6.3: only the abandonment of happiness brought about by that antidote is stated.
sbh4.2:6.5: It is equanimity, mindfulness and clear-knowing.
sbh4.2:6.6: Through repeated practice of this, having moved beyond the third *dhyāna*, he abandons the happiness that belongs to the third-*dhyāna* plane.
sbh4.2:6.7: Therefore he says 'and from the abandonment of happiness'.
sbh4.2:6.8: At that time the contemplator attains the transcendence of pleasure and pain.
sbh4.2:6.9: Summing up both what was previously abandoned and what is now abandoned,
sbh4.2:6.11: 'from the abandonment of happiness, from the abandonment of pain, and from the earlier disappearance of gladness and dejection'.
sbh4.2:6.12: [Restored: Here,] because happiness is abandoned at the time of attaining the fourth *dhyāna*, pain at the time of attaining the second, because gladness disappears at the time of attaining the third and dejection at the time of attaining the first — by now, with happiness and pain abandoned, only neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling [Conjectural: remains] for him.
sbh4.2:6.13: Therefore he says 'neither-painful-nor-pleasant'. At that time all the defects of the lower planes, beginning with the first *dhyāna*, have been abandoned:
sbh4.2:6.14: namely *vitarka* and *vicāra*, rapture, and in-and-out breathing.
sbh4.2:6.15: And through their abandonment, the equanimity there
sbh4.2:6.17: fully purified, so that the mind of one who has attained the fourth *dhyāna* stands firm, immovable,
sbh4.2:6.19: Therefore he says 'pure in equanimity and mindfulness'. Here 'the fourth' is to be understood as before, [Restored: as in the first and the other *dhyāna*s].
sbh4.2:7.1: Of one resolved on space, the perception of colour — connected with blue, yellow, red, white and so on — is transcended [Conjectural: in that it no longer appears, and through disenchantment and dispassion].
sbh4.2:7.2: Therefore he says 'from the transcendence of perceptions of form'. [Restored: From the transcendence of these,] because they go to non-appearance, the perception of obstruction — of many kinds, of many and varied sorts, caused by the accumulation of colour — has vanished too.
sbh4.2:7.3: Therefore he says 'from the disappearance of perceptions of resistance'. And further, because these have vanished, the perceptions based on accumulation that occur with regard to the remaining differentiated aggregates — namely perceptions of food, drink, [Restored: carriage,] clothing, ornament, house, garden, forest, army, mountain and so on —
sbh4.2:7.4: to these no directing of the mind whatever occurs for him.
sbh4.2:7.5: Therefore he says 'from non-attention to perceptions of variety'.
sbh4.2:7.6: Having thus [Conjectural: dispelled] the perceptions of form, resistance and variety, he becomes resolved on space under the aspect of infinity.
sbh4.2:7.7: Therefore he says 'infinite space'. Having passed beyond the preparatory stage (*sāmantaka*), [Restored: after] the practice-culminating attention he attains the basic [attainment] (*maula*), the fruit of practice-culmination.
sbh4.2:7.8: Therefore he says 'he dwells having attained the sphere of infinite space'.
sbh4.2:8.1: As long as he has not attained the basic [attainment],
sbh4.2:8.2: his object is space; but once he has attained it, [his object is] that and the other aggregates of his own plane; in the preparatory stage, the aggregates of lower planes as well.
sbh4.2:8.3: [Conjectural: He — by the consciousness with which] he resolves on infinite space,
sbh4.2:8.4: that very consciousness, which resolves on space under the aspect of infinity —
sbh4.2:8.5: wishing to attain the sphere of infinite consciousness,
sbh4.2:8.6: having turned away the perception of the sphere of infinite space,
sbh4.2:8.7: resolves on that very consciousness under the aspect of infinity.
sbh4.2:8.8: The basic sphere of infinite space, with its preparatory stage, is transcended.
sbh4.2:8.9: Therefore he says 'having completely transcended the sphere of infinite space, "infinite consciousness"'.
sbh4.2:8.10: Having passed beyond the preparatory stage of the sphere of infinite consciousness — up to the practice-culminating attention — he attains the basic [attainment], the fruit of practice-culmination.
sbh4.2:8.11: Therefore he says 'he dwells having attained the sphere of infinite consciousness'.
sbh4.2:9.1: Rising up from the sphere of infinite consciousness, seeking an object beyond consciousness, he does not find one —
sbh4.2:9.2: [any object] connected with anything, with form or formless.
sbh4.2:9.3: Not finding that object, having transcended the basic sphere of infinite consciousness with its preparatory stage, he resolves: 'There is no other object whatever.'
sbh4.2:9.4: He becomes resolved on the perception of nothingness.
sbh4.2:9.5: Through repeated practice of that resolve on the perception, having passed beyond the preparatory stage of the sphere of nothingness — up to the practice-culminating attention — he attains the basic [attainment], the fruit of practice-culmination.
sbh4.2:9.6: Therefore he says 'having completely transcended the sphere of infinite consciousness, "there is nothing", he dwells having attained the sphere of nothingness'.
sbh4.2:10.1: Rising up from the sphere of nothingness,
sbh4.2:10.2: perceiving grossness, perceiving fault in the perception of nothingness, he turns away the perception of the sphere of nothingness.
sbh4.2:10.3: Thereby, previously, at the time of attaining the sphere of nothingness, the perception of [Restored: something] was transcended; now the perception of nothing is transcended.
sbh4.2:10.4: Therefore he says [Conjectural: 'neither perception' — that is, neither the perception of something nor the perception of nothing]. But it is not that all perception whatever has ceased for him,
sbh4.2:10.5: as in the attainment of non-perception or the attainment of cessation; only that this perception is subtle and proceeds on a [Restored: signless] object.
sbh4.2:10.7: Thus resolved on that sphere, having passed beyond the basic sphere of nothingness with its preparatory stage [Restored: and] the preparatory stage of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — up to the practice-culminating attention — he attains the basic [attainment], the fruit of practice-culmination.
sbh4.2:10.8: Therefore he says 'having completely transcended the sphere of nothingness, he dwells having attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception'.
sbh4.2:10.9: There, at the time of *dhyāna* attainment, [the body appears] as if entering Rasātala below —
sbh4.2:10.10: [this is] the sign in the body's appearance;
sbh4.2:10.11: at the time of formless attainment, [Conjectural: as if flying up into the sky].
sbh4.2:10.12: In that case, right practice is to look on [them] with equanimity at the time of *śamatha*.
sbh4.2:12.1: Here, there are two attainments without mind: the attainment of non-perception and the attainment of cessation.
sbh4.2:12.2: Here, only an ordinary person enters the attainment of non-perception, by the attention turned away from perception; but only a noble one [enters] the attainment of cessation.
sbh4.2:12.3: Here, entry into these two attainments is by two attentions:
sbh4.2:12.4: namely, into the attainment of non-perception by the attention turned away from perception; and into the attainment of cessation by the attention that has risen up from neither-perception-nor-non-perception and wholly suppresses the object.
sbh4.2:12.5: Here: 'perception is a disease, perception is a boil, perception is an arrow; this is calm, this is sublime, namely the state of non-perception' —
sbh4.2:12.6: taking up the attention turned away from perception, he practises [Restored: non-mindfulness and non-attention] toward each perception as it arises.
sbh4.2:12.7: Through his cultivation, on the path of preparation, there is a state still with mind;
sbh4.2:12.8: and [Restored: as soon as] he has entered the attainment, mind no longer proceeds.
sbh4.2:12.9: Thus, in one free of passion for the [Restored: Śubhakṛtsna gods] and [Restored: not] free of passion for the Bṛhatphala [gods], the cessation of mind and mental dharmas by an attention preceded by the perception of escape — this is called the attainment of non-perception.
sbh4.2:12.10: And this is how it is obtained.
sbh4.2:12.11: Here, the noble one who has gained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, wishing to dwell in a further calm dwelling, raises his mind up out of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
sbh4.2:12.12: That mind, risen up, does not find an object.
sbh4.2:12.15: Thus, in a trainee free of passion for the sphere of nothingness, or in an arhat, the cessation of mind and mental dharmas by an attention preceded by the perception of dwelling — this is called the attainment of cessation; and this is how it is obtained.
sbh4.2:13.1: Here, the bringing forth of the five higher knowledges occurs with *dhyāna* as its support.
sbh4.2:13.3: In this way: the contemplator becomes a gainer
sbh4.2:13.5: Relying on that pure *dhyāna*, whatever teaching with the higher knowledges as its chief topic he has heard, grasped and mastered — concerning the range of supernatural power, or past abodes, the divine ear, death-and-rebirth, and the ways of [others'] minds — attending to that very [teaching] with the attention of the concentrated plane, he comes to understand the meaning
sbh4.2:13.7: For him who understands the meaning and understands the dharma, shaping his mind thus and thus, through repeated practice
sbh4.2:13.8: there comes a time, an occasion, when the five higher knowledges, the fruits of his cultivation, arise.
sbh4.2:14.1: Moreover, he who thus understands the meaning and understands the dharma cultivates twelve perceptions in order to bring forth all the higher knowledges.
sbh4.2:14.5: the perception of the fusion of body and mind, the perception of resolve,
sbh4.2:14.6: the perception of recollecting in sequence the conduct previously experienced,
sbh4.2:14.7: the perception of the noise of assembled sounds of various kinds, the perception of the [Restored: luminous] form-sign,
sbh4.2:14.8: the perception of changes in form produced by defilements, the perception of [Conjectural: the liberations], the perception of the bases of mastery, and the perception of the totalities.
sbh4.2:15.1: Here, in the perception of lightness, he resolves on himself as light,
sbh4.2:15.2: like a [Restored: tuft] of cotton-wool or a [Restored: tuft] of kapok
sbh4.2:15.3: in a whirlwind. Resolving thus, he impels [himself] there by the attention of resolve itself,
sbh4.2:15.4: as from the couch [Conjectural: to the stool], from the stool to the couch,
sbh4.2:15.5: and so from the couch [Conjectural: to the grass-mat], from the grass-mat to the couch.
sbh4.2:15.7: he resolves on the body as soft,
sbh4.2:15.8: like [Restored: silk], [Restored: raw silk], or [Restored: woven silk].
sbh4.2:15.9: Thus this perception of softness nourishes and supports the perception of lightness, whereby the perception of lightness, so supported, comes to extension, growth and abundance.
sbh4.2:15.10: Here, the perception of the space-element: by this perception he resolves on his own lightness and softness.
sbh4.2:15.11: If he wishes to go somewhere,
sbh4.2:15.12: whatever material thing lies in between and obstructs his going, he resolves to be space,
sbh4.2:15.14: Here, the perception of the fusion of mind and body: by which he fuses the mind into the body,
sbh4.2:15.15: or the body into the mind, whereby his body becomes lighter, softer, more workable, more luminous,
sbh4.2:15.16: conforming to mind, bound to mind, proceeding in dependence on mind.
sbh4.2:15.17: Here, the perception of resolve: by which perception he resolves on the far as near, the near as far, the small as large, the large as small, earth as water, water as earth — thus with each great element in respect of the other, in full.
sbh4.2:15.18: Likewise he also resolves on magical creations, whether creations of form or creations of sound.
sbh4.2:15.19: By these five perceptions, perfected through cultivation, he experiences the range of supernatural power of many kinds: being one, he displays himself as many —
sbh4.2:15.20: namely, by the perception of resolve on creation; then, having displayed himself as many, he becomes one —
sbh4.2:15.21: namely, by the perception of resolve on the disappearance of the creation; he passes through walls, [Restored: through mountains,] through ramparts with body unhindered;
sbh4.2:15.23: he emerges from and plunges into the earth
sbh4.2:15.24: as if in water; on water he goes with the stream parting [before him], as if on earth;
sbh4.2:15.25: he travels through the sky cross-legged,
sbh4.2:15.26: like a winged bird; and he rubs with his hand these sun and moon, so mighty, so powerful,
sbh4.2:15.28: Up to the Brahmā world he wields power with his body.
sbh4.2:15.29: All this he does by the perception of resolve, assisted by the perceptions of lightness, softness, the space-element, and the fusion of mind and body.
sbh4.2:15.30: [This] is to be understood as appropriate.
sbh4.2:15.31: Here, the wielding of power over the Brahmā world with the body is twofold:
sbh4.2:15.33: and, [Restored: by resolve as he wishes,] over [Restored: the four great elements] below the Brahmā world and over a part of derived form.
sbh4.2:15.34: Here, the perception of recollecting in sequence the conduct previously experienced: by which, from the state of childhood onward, wherever his memory proceeds
sbh4.2:15.36: wherever he has gone, stood, sat or lain — recollecting in detail all the conduct he previously experienced, [Conjectural: in gross outline, in due sequence and without skipping], he recognizes it.
sbh4.2:15.37: Through cultivation of this, as the fruit of cultivation he recollects his manifold past abodes, up through *saṁsāra*, with their particulars, in full.
sbh4.2:15.38: Here, the perception of the noise of assembled sounds of various kinds:
sbh4.2:15.39: in whatever village, town, guild, corporation, assembly, spacious house or chamber the mingled, varied noise of a crowd of people of various kinds, seated and assembled, issues forth,
sbh4.2:15.40: which is called the sound of hubbub,
sbh4.2:15.41: or the noise of a great river in flood — grasping the sign there, the cultivation of the perception by which, with the attention of the concentrated plane, he [Conjectural: fixes] his mental focus on sounds noble and ignoble, divine and human, far and near.
sbh4.2:15.42: Through repeated practice of it, he gains the divine ear as the fruit of cultivation,
sbh4.2:15.43: by which he hears divine and human sounds,
sbh4.2:15.44: both those far and those near.
sbh4.2:15.45: Here, the perception of the luminous form-sign:
sbh4.2:15.46: as before, grasping the sign of light, he attends to that very sign. [Restored: And grasping the sign from the variety of beings, he attends to that very sign, distinguishing by the performance of wholesome and unwholesome deeds and the like.]
sbh4.2:15.47: This is the perception of the luminous form-sign.
sbh4.2:15.48: Through cultivation of it, he gains the knowledge of death-and-rebirth as the fruit of cultivation,
sbh4.2:15.49: by which, 'with the purified divine eye' — in full, up to — '[beings] at the breakup of the body are reborn in a [Restored: good destination], in a heavenly world, among the gods'.
sbh4.2:15.50: Here, the perception of changes in form produced by defilements:
sbh4.2:15.51: by which he observes the bodily condition of beings who are lustful, hateful and deluded, whose minds are enwrapped by the defilements and secondary defilements anger, enmity, [Restored: concealment], burning, [Restored: deceit, dissimulation,] shamelessness and lack of dread of blame,
sbh4.2:15.53: Such is the bodily condition of one who is lustful,
sbh4.2:15.55: namely, agitated senses, [Restored: excited senses,] a smiling face.
sbh4.2:15.56: Such is the bodily condition of one who is hateful,
sbh4.2:15.58: namely, a pale face, a stammering voice,
sbh4.2:15.60: Such is the bodily condition of one who is deluded,
sbh4.2:15.62: namely, muteness, inability to grasp a meaning when it is pondered, and [Conjectural: vulgar] speech.
sbh4.2:15.63: By these aspects and the like — up through one enwrapped by shamelessness and lack of dread of blame — whatever bodily condition there is,
sbh4.2:15.65: grasping the sign from that, he attends [to it].
sbh4.2:15.66: Through repeated practice of it, the knowledge of the ways of [others'] minds arises as the fruit of cultivation,
sbh4.2:15.67: by which he knows with his own mind, as it actually is, the mind of other beings and other persons, with what it thinks and ponders.
sbh4.2:15.68: Here, the cultivation of the perceptions of the liberations, the bases of mastery and the totalities is to be understood as before,
sbh4.2:15.70: By this cultivation he brings forth noble supernatural power —
sbh4.2:15.71: [the power] of transforming things, of creation, of resolve —
sbh4.2:15.72: and likewise *araṇā*, the knowledge from resolve,
sbh4.2:15.73: and the four discriminations: the discrimination of dharma, the discrimination of meaning, the discrimination of language, and the discrimination of expression.
sbh4.2:16.1: Here, this is the distinction between noble and ignoble supernatural power:
sbh4.2:16.2: by noble supernatural power, whatever thing he transforms,
sbh4.2:16.3: whatever [Restored: creation] he creates, [Conjectural: whatever he resolves on,]
sbh4.2:16.6: and with all of it the [intended] work can be done.
sbh4.2:16.7: By ignoble [supernatural power], on the other hand, it does not become so; rather,
sbh4.2:16.8: only a mere show appears, as of an illusionist.
